pageCache.pageTitle: British Values at Shenstone School - Shenstone School
pageCache.text:
British Values at Shenstone School
At Shenstone School, we are committed to embedding the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs into every aspect of our school life. These values are interwoven within our own school ethos and curriculum, ensuring that our pupils are supported to understand these principles through their experiences, and develop them throughout their educational journey.
Integrating British Values into Our Ethos and Curriculum
Democracy Our pupils are encouraged to participate in democratic processes, such as participation in our school council, and informing whole school decisions and practices as well as fostering a sense of self advocacy and responsibility.
The Rule of Law Our school promotes understanding of the importance of rules, whether they govern the class, the school, or the country. This is scaffolded by our behaviour policies, whole school focus on wellbeing and supporting our learners to understand their rights and responsibilities at home, in school and within the wider community.
Individual Liberty Our pupils are encouraged to make choices within a safe and supportive environment. We provide opportunities for them to express their interests and opinions, promoting self-confidence and self-awareness using their preferred communication style.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance Respect is a core value at Shenstone School. We celebrate diversity and encourage our pupils to understand and appreciate cultures, faiths, and beliefs different from their own through assemblies, curriculum opportunities, cultural and enrichment events.
Supporting Pupils to Understand and Develop British Values
Our approach includes:
Curriculum Integration: British values are embedded across subjects, enabling pupils to explore these concepts in various contexts.
Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural Development (SMSC): We provide a range of activities and experiences that promote personal development and understanding of the wider world.
Assemblies and Celebrations: Regular assemblies and events focus on themes related to British values, fostering a shared understanding and community spirit.
Pupil Voice: We value our pupils' opinions and provide platforms for them to express their views through our Total Communication approach, contributing to school improvement and fostering a sense of belonging.
Through these initiatives, Shenstone School ensures that pupils not only learn about British values but also live them, preparing them to be respectful, responsible, and active members of society.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
We strive to implement learning support systems and strategies that meet the holistic development and learning needs of our amazing pupils at Shenstone School.
Every child is an individual, and as such, we diligently work as a school team and with wider multi-agency support teams to ensure that our curriculum delivery recognises this individual support, supporting each child with their life-long learning journey.
Shenstone School is an all-through school for children with severe or complex learning difficulties within the London Borough of Bexley. All pupils who attend Shenstone School have Education and Health Care Plans. We are one of two special schools within The Kemnal Academies Trust (TKAT).
Shenstone School is based across three sites: Sidcup, Crayford and Belvedere. From the academic year 2026-2027, we can accommodate pupils up to Year 11, and we will continue to add an additional year group until we reach year 13 making us all through (Reception to Year 13), across our three school sites.
Paramount to our ethos is the belief in “support for all”, which ensures that engagement with the pupils, their families, and our staff team is at the heart of all that we strive to achieve. We work hard to ensure that Shenstone is a safe, happy, welcoming, and truly outstanding place where our pupils will thrive. Our school benefits from impressive facilities across all school sites, enabling us to offer a wide range of opportunities and activities to enhance learning both inside and outside the classroom.
"Trees grow and so do we"
..when asked about why the Shenstone Logo has a tree...
Our pupils are amazing, and their progress is inspiring. Regardless of how big or small their successes are, we are very proud of the children and pleased to contribute to and support their achievements. The values and ethos of "together we engage, thrive, and achieve" are entwined through all that we do at Shenstone School.
As the Executive Head Teacher of Shenstone School, I am truly privileged to work with such fantastic children and to be part of a dedicated staff team.
We hope you enjoy your visit to our website, which aims to give you a glimpse into our busy school life and provide regularly updated information.
TKAT commissioned for a video to be made to showcase Shenstone, please click on the link below to see the finished product!

This past year, we have worked hard to earn the Leading Parents Partnership Award and have kept you updated along the way.
We are pleased to let you know our final assessment will take place on Tuesday 6th October. Earning this award shows our dedication to building strong, positive connections between home and school.
Thank you for being so supportive, whether you filled out a survey, came to an event, or shared your ideas.
We look forward to showing the assessor the strong partnership we have built and will continue to develop.
We had our interim assessor visit on 13th February and our initial objectives were signed off. We are continuing to work towards achieving this award and will keep you updated on our progress. Thank you for your ongoing support, we very much appreciate this. 'Together we engage, thrive and achieve.'
We have taken Parents feedback on board and created more opportunities to come and visit the school and lessons, e.g. open Christmas, open Primary days, EYFS projects.
Based on the parental feedback, we have created the action plan and are working towards achieving green in all areas.
The advisor will be visiting Shenstone school on the 13th of February to review the evidence and provide the next steps for development.

pageCache.text:
Ofsted and Challenge Partners
Shenstone Accountability
As a school, we would be expected to publish pupil progress. In our case the thresholds are rarely met by Shenstone pupils due to their cognitive ability and where it has, the number would be too low to publish and would be suppressed.
Having said this, our pupils at Shenstone School are amazing superstars who work very hard to achieve small and big steps of progress over time. They are supported by a dedicated staff team and we stand by our motto of “together we engage, thrive and achieve".
Shenstone School was inspected in June 2025 and the outcome is that we are outstanding in all areas.
"Pupils are happy and eager to start their day in this safe and welcoming school. Staff have created a safe and nurturing atmosphere that celebrates pupils’ special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). There is no ceiling to the ambition staff have for the pupils in their care. Skilled staff provide a range of learning activities and experiences that best support pupils with complex needs. Staff, parents and carers, work together to enable pupils to ‘engage, thrive and achieve’."
"Staff are vigilant and watch pupils’ behaviour closely. Routines are well embedded in the school. Staff teach pupils to develop autonomy through high-quality play and interactive experiences. The early years provides an exceptionally strong foundation for children’s learning and development."
"Pupils enjoy a wide range of opportunities to support their wider personal development. A holistic approach to pupils’ development sits at the centre of the curriculum. The curriculum provides pupils with the knowledge and skills they need to function in adulthood and to access the community, with increasing independence."
"Staff help pre-verbal pupils to ‘find their voice’. Pupils express themselves using a range of equipment and technology. Older pupils share their views about how to improve the school through the school council."
Our last OFSTED inspection was 18-19 June 2025, see the last OFSTED Report at the bottom of the page.
Please find below relevant information from the Department for Education Performance Tables.
https://www.compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk/school/144041/shenstone-school
It is a three-day, rigorous peer evaluation of teaching and learning, curriculum and outcomes, and leadership at all levels. It has a sharp focus on the experience of pupils from disadvantaged backgrounds or with additional needs.
The mission is to reduce educational inequality and improve the life chances of all children. Through collaboration, challenge and leadership development, they are working to ensure every school community can benefit from the combined wisdom of the education system.
Each school hosts an annual review, and reciprocates by sending their senior leaders to review other schools in the network, providing continuous professional development for all leaders involved.
The latest Challenge partner report is at the bottom of the page.
We are delighted to report that it was a very positive experience and the children and staff team highlighted Shenstone spirit with great examples of work and play across the Challenge Partners visit days.

Community Links
At Shenstone School we are invested in our local community and we take pride in our local area
Our children across all 3 sites took part in this year's harvest festivities. Children at our Sidcup site had an immersive day of harvest themed activities. At Crayford, pupils took part in a harvest performance that parents thoroughly enjoyed. At Belvedere, our secondary pupil spent time collating and sorting the harvest donations from all sites and pupils met with Kate, the representative from the Bexley Food Bank, who collected the 75.5 kilograms of donations in what will hopefully be the start of a wonderful partnership!
Dear Valued Supporter,
Bexley Foodbank would like to take this opportunity to say from the bottom of our hearts a huge thank you to you all.
Your donations really do make a difference to the lives of people experiencing food poverty in Bexley.
It’s been an incredible Harvest and our volunteers have worked their socks off receiving, sorting and dating the food coming in and the following numbers are staggering!
In total we received 7798.42 kilos!!! (287.95 out of date).
Your collection contributed to 75.5kg
Bexley Foodbank give out on average 5000kg every month to those most in need, so this gives you an idea of the scale of food poverty.
We feel incredibly blessed by you all, your kindness is unmatched.
Blessings to you all.
Graham Wakefield from Bexley Voice was our guest speaker at our 'Preparing for Adulthood, Understanding Deputyship' Workshop in March 2026 which was very well received and appreciated by our parents who attended.
Graham has kindly agreed to do this for us again in the future. Dawn Lyman, our Family Wellbeing Liaison organised this event with Bexley Voice.
Millie from the Continence Team supports our Families and is also joining us for a Continence Workshop in May 2026.

PE and Sports
MOVE at Shenstone School
MOVE’s (Movement Opportunities Via Education) aim is to further develop students skills in functional sitting, standing, walking and transitions whilst accessing the curriculum and learning opportunities.
In Shenstone School MOVE celebrates what our children are able to do already and looks to build upon these foundations. With the support of parents/carers, class staff and other professionals, we as a multi-disciplinary team work together to agree meaningful goals which promote the student’s confidence and independence. Each goal is specific to the individual and could be holding their head up to indicate preference to kicking a ball to play with their siblings.
Each program is specifically tailored to the individual and is then embedded into their daily routine at school. This allows for the child to practice their new skills and ensure they are integrated into their daily life.

Pupil Premium
What is the pupil premium?
Pupil premium is funding to improve education outcomes for disadvantaged pupils in schools in England. Evidence shows that disadvantaged children generally face additional challenges in reaching their potential at school and often do not perform as well as other pupils.
Pupil premium at Shenstone?
All pupils at Shenstone School present with severe or complex learning needs, including some children who may have more profound or medical needs. Shenstone School is a specialist school that supports the learning and development needs of pupils with an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP). The pupils at Shenstone School are all disadvantaged due to their severe learning difficulties; some may also be disadvantaged due to their socioeconomic circumstances. The school receives pupil premium funding to improve social and educational outcomes for these pupils.
Barriers to learning are primarily developmental, focusing on enabling pupils to acquire communication, independence, physical, regulation and social skills within the school, home and the wider community. Our strategy is underpinned by evidence-informed research, focusing on removing barriers to learning through targeted support and providing early and ongoing intervention for pupils and their families.
Intended outcomes
This explains the outcomes we aim for by the end of our current strategic plan and how we will measure whether the outcomes have been achieved.
Families feel supported and able to meet their children’s complex needs - Ensure children and families have high-quality support and advice, and where needed, families are supported to access external services and benefits. FWL to become an ACE tutor. Families are given opportunities to engage in informal and structured learning opportunities.
Targeted pupils have access to high-quality tutoring, which supports them to make accelerated progress in reading - Literacy Tutor to support targeted Pupils /Students working at both pre-reading and reading skills, including phonics.
Children regulate their sensory systems which positively impact on their behaviour and ability to learn, in school, at home and in the wider community - Children with identified sensory processing issues or dysregulation access provision coordinated through the additional OT time purchased.
All Year 6 pupils will have the opportunity to access a one-night residential - Year 6 pupils will attend a one-night residential where they will engage in a range of high-quality experiences that enable them to generalise understanding and provide opportunities to develop practical and independent skills.
Targeted support and interventions enable pupils to use a range of communication systems to aid their understanding and to develop expressive and purposeful communication in school, at home, and in the community - ACE Tutor (communication) to use Universal, targeted and specialist interventions offered to enhance the curriculum to provide opportunities for increased engagement, enjoyment, attention, motivation and spontaneous communication in school and the community.
Universal, targeted and specialist interventions offered to enhance the curriculum to provide opportunities for increased engagement, enjoyment, attention, motivation and spontaneous communication in school and the community - Specialist Music teacher Tutoring for targeted groups from a SEND Drama / Music specialist two days per week to enrich children’s learning through music and drama. The learning focus supports engagement and communication that they may have missed out on during the pandemic. Offering additional support opportunities to increase attention levels will benefit the children being supported.
Pupils’ learning is not affected by hunger. Targeted pupils explore/eat different breakfast foods - Through our observations and from staff feedback, we have recognised a reduction in behaviour issues around food in the morning since beginning the Magic breakfast initiative.
